topics.topic: Terminal conditions selecting ServiceExit members and their process exit statuses
questions: Which complete process histories and termination conditions produce each member, including clean shutdown, failure before listening, failure while serving, and forced or externally requested termination?
What success or failure exit-status semantics correspond to `start_failed`, `served` and `server_failed`, and must the two failure members be externally distinguishable?
What terminal facts cause the service to mint each ServiceExit member, and which process exit status does each member select?
What terminal process condition selects each of `start_failed`, `served` and `server_failed`, including whether a clean stop before serving any request counts as `served` or `server_failed`?

quotes:
`EXIT_STATUSES` holds exactly one row for each member of = models.ServiceExit, keyed by `outcome`; a
member without its row stops the build. The service has begun listening once its web server reports
its startup complete, its socket accepting connections; that report is the boundary. = models.ServiceExit
is START_FAILED, value `start_failed`: the process ends before that boundary, whatever ends it, a signal
included; SERVED, value `served`: after it, a SIGINT or SIGTERM stops the web server, which returns without
an error, and nothing fails until the process ends; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it, the
process ends in any other way, a failure during or after the shutdown of a stopped server included, so any
failure after the boundary outranks the signal.

| `outcome` | `status` |
|---|---|
| `START_FAILED` | 1 |
| `SERVED` | 0 |
| `SERVER_FAILED` | 1 |
judgement.why: State 2 defines the listening boundary, every terminal condition selecting each member, and the resulting process statuses, including that both failure members select status 1.

topics.topic: ServiceExit representation as a model, runtime type, or process-control constant
questions: Must ServiceExit become a `kind: enum` model, a later contract_only runtime type, or a non-model process-control constant?
The passage must become a `models` entry with `kind: "enum"` instead of excluding this enumeration from the models of State 1.

quotes:
`EXIT_STATUSES` holds exactly one row for each member of = models.ServiceExit, keyed by `outcome`; a
member without its row stops the build. The service has begun listening once its web server reports
its startup complete, its socket accepting connections; that report is the boundary. = models.ServiceExit
is START_FAILED, value `start_failed`: the process ends before that boundary, whatever ends it, a signal
included; SERVED, value `served`: after it, a SIGINT or SIGTERM stops the web server, which returns without
an error, and nothing fails until the process ends; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it, the
process ends in any other way, a failure during or after the shutdown of a stopped server included, so any
failure after the boundary outranks the signal.
judgement.why: The later texts place ServiceExit in domain_models and refer to it explicitly as models.ServiceExit with a closed set of named values; the quoted SPEC_STANDARD rule only restricts records that are placed in models and does not require every enumeration mentioned during State 1 to be declared there immediately.

topics.topic: Actions that produce and consume ServiceExit
questions: Which product action creates the ServiceExit value, from which termination fact, and which action reads it to choose the process exit status?

quotes: run_service: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call load_runtime_settings, then load_config with those settings, then read_token with the credential_file of the settings as a Path, then the imported create_app with that context and token, in that order, and serve the application with the imported uvicorn on the host of the imported BIND_HOST constant and the port of the settings, trusting no forwarded or proxy header. It MUST return the status of the row of the imported EXIT_STATUSES constant for the member of = models.ServiceExit the way the process ends: the START_FAILED member when any step or a signal ends it before the web server listens, after writing one line naming the failed step to standard error and never the token; the SERVED member when its web server returns after a SIGINT or SIGTERM stopped it; and the SERVER_FAILED member for any other end after the web server has begun listening.
judgement.why: The later orchestration note assigns both selection of the ServiceExit member from the terminal fact and lookup of its process status to run_service.
